- The system consists of a foam agent tank with a capacity of 20,000 litres, from which foam paths run to diesel tanks 1 and 2 through the pump installed after the foam tank; the tanks are also cooled by water sprinklers distributed over each tank.
The first draft was prepared by Eng. Ahmed Mohamed El-Mohtady Qamra, tested by Eng. Abdel Meguid El-Henawy, and reviewed by
Eng. El-Said Shaaban Abdel Qader, accepted by Eng. Magdy Okba, General Manager of Boiler Maintenance, and approved by Eng. Ahmed Abdel Meguid Sawan, Head of El-Nubaria Power Station Sector.

The document was reviewed by Chemist Ibrahim Youssef Youssef, Occupational Safety and Health Inspector in the Inspection Sector, and approved by Eng. rows: Issue an approved work order from the competent authority; those carrying out the maintenance work must hold an occupational safety and health category card.
Cordon off the area to define the work area, and place warning signs.
Follow the occupational safety and health procedures for personnel and equipment, and wear personal protective equipment (safety helmet, safety shoes, overalls, gloves .....)
Complete tool bag
Cleaning fluids
Make sure the fire-fighting system is in service.
Check all the main procedures of the system.
Make sure the site is prepared for carrying out the test and draining the water.
Define the work area, cordon it off, and place the appropriate warning signs.
Make sure the gauges are in good condition and read correctly.
Make sure the foam tank level is suitable for carrying out the test.
Make sure all the valves on the foam line are open and in good condition.
Make sure the water pressure before the deluge valve is suitable for carrying out the test.
Make sure the fire-fighting water path with the foam agent is diverted outside the tank by opening the nearest flange from the tank side.
Test the thermal detector by raising its temperature to 108°C and making sure the system operates automatically.
Test the manual start of the system.
Make sure the fire alarm sound is heard on the tank, and record the time until the alarm sound is heard on the fire system monitoring panel.
Make sure all the alarms work correctly.
Make sure the deluge valve opens correctly.
Make sure the cooling water comes out onto the tank body.
Make sure all the sprinklers are sound and work well.
Make sure all the sprinklers are aimed correctly to cool the tank body.
Make sure the foam fire-fighting system is operating.
Make sure of the foam-to-water mixing ratio (within 3%).
Make sure of the water pressure during the test and that it does not reach the minimum operating limit (10 bar).
Make sure the alarm for sending water to the tank works on the fire panel ACP-012.
Close the main water valve (before the deluge valve).
Make sure the main drain valve works.
Make sure the auxiliary drain valve works.
Make sure the alarm for water discharge from the tank has disappeared from the fire panel ACP-012.
Return the manual start lever of the system.
Return the deluge valve to its position before operating the system (closed position).
Open the main water valve before (the deluge valve).
Make sure the deluge valve is closed and make sure of the water pressure before the valve.
Return the foam fire-fighting system path to inside the tank.
Check the foam tank level.
Observe all the main parts of the system and make sure they are in good condition.
Make sure all the gauges work well.
Make sure the fire-fighting system monitoring panel works well and clear all the alarms on the panel.
Remove the cordoning and warning signs from the work area.
Make sure the system is in service.

Introduction
This document outlines the steps of the annual inspection of the fire-fighting and cooling system on the diesel tanks.
- The system consists of a foam agent tank with a capacity of 20,000 litres, from which foam paths run to diesel tanks 1 and 2 through the pump installed after the foam tank; the tanks are also cooled by water sprinklers distributed over each tank.
The first draft was prepared by Eng. Ahmed Mohamed El-Mohtady Qamra, tested by Eng. Abdel Meguid El-Henawy, and reviewed by
Eng. El-Said Shaaban Abdel Qader, accepted by Eng. Magdy Okba, General Manager of Boiler Maintenance, and approved by Eng. Ahmed Abdel Meguid Sawan, Head of El-Nubaria Power Station Sector.
The document was reviewed by Chemist Ibrahim Youssef Youssef, Occupational Safety and Health Inspector in the Inspection Sector, and approved by Eng. Samir Abdel Gelil, General Manager of Inspection and Quality Control at the Middle Delta Electricity Production Company and the company's Maintenance Procedure Information System coordinator, and certified by Eng. Mohamed Naguib Abdel Hay, Head of the Inspection and Quality Control Sector at the Middle Delta Electricity Production Company.
Safety Precautions
Issue an approved work order from the competent authority; those carrying out the maintenance work must hold an occupational safety and health category card. | 
Cordon off the area to define the work area, and place warning signs. |

uncertain_terms.note: Header says 'Transformer Stations' although the equipment is the diesel-tank fire-fighting system; translated verbatim as in the source.
'السولار' is diesel fuel in Egyptian usage; translated as 'diesel tanks'.
Manufacturer name transliterated from 'موللر'; spelling not verified against the original document.
Source shows '20,\000' with a stray backslash; read as 20,000 litres.
Garbled temperature in source ('حتيcه 108'); read as 'up to 108°C'.
Step 2 says 'الإجراءات الرئيسية' (procedures) where the companion document FS-063 says 'الأجزاء الرئيسية' (parts); translated verbatim as in the source.
'التصفية' read as drain (تصريف) by intent; translated as 'drain valve'.
Source shows corrupted characters ('ب��ف التصفية'); read as 'بلف التصفية' (drain valve).
Source omits the preposition ('خروج المياه التنك'); read as water discharge from the tank.
Footer field says 'Breaker code' on a fire-system document; translated verbatim as in the source.
'8April 2009' in the source; rendered as '8 April 2009'.
